title: Legendary Pawn: Hold the Rook Ending
summary: Once the attack has simplified to a drawable ending, recover material with check and avoid exposing the pawn.

nodes.question: Black has taken the bishop. Can White recover material without losing?
nodes.explanation: The bishop on h5 stands in front of Kh6 on the rook’s file. Rxh5+ removes it with check and reaches an exact draw. The e6 pawn has already disappeared; White’s king is on e6, not d6.

branches.title: Source sideline: recover the bishop with check
commentary: Begin after ...Rxf1 in the complete saved 26-second diagram. This is the source’s illustrated mistake sideline, now an exact drawing objective rather than a claim that the earlier attack was verified.
Rxh5+ captures the bishop and checks Kh6. White recovers material and keeps the exact draw; a rook and pawn remain on each side.
Kg6 steps out of the h-file check. White’s g4 pawn protects Rh5, so the king cannot simply take the rook. The exact ending is drawn with best play; equal material alone is not the proof.
branches.explanation: Kg6 steps out of the h-file check. White’s g4 pawn protects Rh5, so the king cannot simply take the rook. The exact ending is drawn with best play; equal material alone is not the proof.

branches.title: Independent mistake: push instead of taking the bishop
commentary: Compare a pawn check that leaves Black’s extra bishop on the board.
g5+ gives up the draw. White has not removed Bh5 and has advanced the pawn into Black’s king’s reach.
Kg6 escapes the check and attacks g5. Black keeps the bishop and an exact winning position; checking first has not solved White’s material problem.

exercises.prompt: Why capture with the rook before pushing again?
exercises.answer: Rxh5+ removes Black’s bishop with check and preserves the draw. In this exact diagram g5+ loses with best defense.

exercises.prompt: Does one rook and one pawn each guarantee a draw?
exercises.answer: No. Here the complete positions have exact drawing results. White still needs to keep the rook safe and coordinate the king and pawn.
